source.title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q, α, β) on (0,1), given by -y''(x) + q(x)y(x) = λy(x) with real-valued q in L¹(0,1) and boundary conditions y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0 and y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0. Fix b in (1/2,1]. If one knows a subset of the nodal set of eigenfunctions inside (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there, is that weaker dense nodal data still sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse nodal problem for Sturm-Liouville operators

evidence.quote: Open problem I: It is open if the boundary parameter α = α can be determined by a dense subset of the nodal set in (0, b) but not necessarily by an s-dense subset of the nodal set in (0, b).

Remark 3.1: In [6], Cheng et al. improved Yang’s theorem (Theorem 2.1 in [19]) by weakening s-dense conditions instead of dense conditions. The open problem I is answered affirmatively by Cheng et al. (see Theorem 3.2 in [6]).

accepted.question_text: For the same Sturm-Liouville inverse nodal setting, Yang's uniqueness theorem concerns nodal data in a subinterval (0,b) with b > 1/2. The open question asks whether the corresponding uniqueness conclusion remains valid when the observed nodal data are only in a left subinterval with b in (0,1/2]; that is, whether a twin nodal subset in (0,b) satisfying the same inverse-nodal setup can still determine the potential and boundary data when the observation interval does not extend past 1/2.
accepted.context_brief: Subinterval threshold in inverse nodal uniqueness

evidence.quote: Open problem II: It remains open if the result in Theorem 1.2 holds true for b ∈ (0, 1/2].
This answers an open question of Yang concerning the inverse nodal problem: a dense and twin subset of nodal points in (0, b) (for any fixed b < 1/2 ) does not determine the potential.

For b = 1/2, a uniqueness theorem on inverse nodal problems reads as follows. Theorem 4.3: Assume that ... The nodal set B(A, 1/2, q, α, β) is twin and dense in (0, 1/2), and if there are jk and nk such that ... then (q − ⟨q⟩, α, β)=(q̄ − ⟨q̄⟩, ᾱ, β̄).
